_readme: Built-in channels for Kawasaki ECUs (KWP2000 over K-line, ECU address 0x11 or 0x28). The PWC Scan phone apps use the same file and format.
pid: hex local identifier sent as '21 <pid>'. every: read on every Nth update (1 = every time).
formula variables: A B C D... (data bytes), raw, sraw, n, d. Functions: abs min max round signed(v,bits) math.*
verified: set true once a channel's scaling has been checked against a known-good reading.
gauge_min / gauge_max: range of the tile's gauge bar. null = scale to the values seen this session.
priority: phone apps only. true reads the channel on every update, ahead of the rest, for gauges that need to track faster than 'every' alone allows. Ignored by the Windows app.
defaults_revision: raise it when these channels change in a way users should pick up; defaults_note says what changed. Apps that keep an editable copy offer the new defaults once.

These are the 2007 Ultra LX's scalings, and the default for any ski the apps don't recognise. Other models have their own file (kawasaki_<model>.json): scalings such as oil temp and throttle differ between them. detect: the ECU's answers that identify this model at connect.
defaults_note: Oil Temp (0x98) scaling corrected from raw-40 to raw-119: the old formula read ~100 C on a stone-cold engine. Confirmed 2026-10-21/23 on a 2007 Ultra LX by unplug test and a hose warm-up.

pids.name: Engine RPM
pids.notes: Was 'raw' with no scaling (unverified default). At base idle on a 2007 Ultra LX, raw read 306 while the ski's actual idle is ~1200 rpm — 306 * 4 = 1224, a close match. This ECU appears to store RPM in units of 4 rpm per count (opposite of standard OBD-II's PID 0x0C, which divides by 4). Confirmed at one data point (idle); would be good to confirm at a second RPM (e.g. a brief rev) to rule out a non-multiplicative offset.

pids.name: Throttle sensor
pids.notes: Ultra LX: closed = 246 and wide open = 912 counts (about 1.2 V and 4.5 V if 10-bit at 5 V). Use Capture 0 % / 100 % in Edit to set your own ski's values. Carries over to a 2024 SXR160: a 2026-10-16 key-on/engine-off log moving the throttle lever by hand 0-100% read 247 counts closed and 884-885 at full lever travel, close enough to the Ultra LX's 246/912 that no formula change is needed. 884-885 may be short of true mechanical WOT since this was a hand sweep with the engine off, not a full-throttle pull under load. 2026-10-21 SXR160 idle/rev log: 247-248 counts at idle with the engine running (shows 0.15-0.30 %), 737 on a quick blip to 4300 rpm. Set your own closed value with Capture 0 % if the idle offset bothers you.

pids.name: Intake Pressure
pids.notes: This ski has only one physical pressure sensor (in the intake manifold) — no separate barometric sensor. PID 0x05 is that live reading: in a 2026-10-13 idle/rev research log it read ~101.7 kPa at key-on/engine-off (atmospheric), dropped to ~58 kPa once the engine started and settled into idle (manifold vacuum), then rose to ~79 kPa during a rev to 4284 rpm (vacuum partially collapsing). PID 0x08 previously held this channel but was found frozen at a constant 101.8 kPa for the entire session regardless of engine/RPM state — a dead/duplicate register — and was removed. every bumped from 10 to 1 since this is a fast-changing signal, not a slow one like true barometric pressure, then set to 3 (2026-10-19) so RPM and throttle get more of the bus. Also checks out on a 2024 SXR160: a 2026-10-16 key-on/engine-off log read 836-837 counts (103.66-103.79 kPa, a sane atmospheric value), and 0x08 again mirrored 0x05 exactly at every sample — the same dead/duplicate-register pattern as the Ultra LX. Still need an idle/rev or water-test log on this ski to confirm 0x05 actually drops into vacuum range once the engine runs. Confirmed 2026-10-21 (SXR160, on the trailer, cold, 20-30 s runs): 103.7 kPa engine off, 71-78 kPa just after each start, then 80-94 kPa at a 1060-1630 rpm idle; one sample of 47 kPa about 0.3 s after a blip to 4300 rpm. 0x08 stayed at 836 counts (103.7 kPa) while 0x05 moved, so on this ski 0x08 looks like a stored barometric reading rather than a mirror. The idle values are well above the ~58 kPa idle in the 2026-10-13 log; whether that is the cold, short runs, electronic throttle idle control or something on this ski is not known yet. Needs a warm idle log to compare.

pids.name: Engine temp
pids.notes: Reads degrees C plus 40 (62 = 22 C = 72 F in a 70 F garage). One point only: check against an infrared thermometer once it's warm. Units of C make it switchable between C and F. Seen on a 2007 Ultra LX with key on and engine off. Check on your own ski. A 2026-10-13 water test on another ski showed this channel staying a sane 59-70 C through a sustained 6000+ rpm run while that ski threw an OILH (oil temp high) warning — so on that ECU at least, 0x06 is not the oil sensor; see PID 0x98 below. Also read a sane ambient value on a 2024 SXR160 at key-on/engine-off (60 counts = 20 C, 2026-10-16 log) — consistent with this formula, though unconfirmed under heat on this ski. 2026-10-21 SXR160 idle runs: rose 20 -> 76 C over about 1.5 minutes of total running on the trailer, and kept climbing for a minute or so after each shutdown (heat soak).

pids.name: IAT
pids.notes: Intake Air Temperature (renamed from Intake air temp, 2026-10-19). Same encoding as engine temp. Seen on a 2007 Ultra LX with key on and engine off. Check on your own ski. Also sane on a 2024 SXR160 at key-on/engine-off (61 counts = 21 C, 2026-10-16 log).

pids.name: Oil Temp
pids.notes: 0x98 = oil temperature, CONFIRMED on a 2007 Ultra LX (2026-10-21): unplugging the sensor moved this channel and set off the OILH dash warning; replugging returned it to baseline and the fault self-cleared on runtime, so the sensor is healthy. Raw is 2 bytes 00 XX, higher = hotter; open circuit reads raw 0x64 (100, the ECU's fail-safe substitute). The old raw-40 formula was wrong for this channel: it showed ~99-102 C on a stone-cold, day-sat engine (coolant and IAT both ~20 C at the same time). The scaling is raw - 119, fit 2026-10-23 from a hose warm-up: day-sat cold raw 139 -> 20 C (matched coolant/IAT); warm-up start raw 142 -> 23 C (matched IAT 22); after ~3 min raw 156 -> 37 C — a sensible gradual climb while coolant sat at 36 C on the cold-water hose. Slope ~1 C/count, same as coolant (0x06), just a different offset on this channel. Still worth one infrared-thermometer check at the oil tank once warm to lock the last degree. NOTE the earlier raw-40 story (2026-10-13 OILH water test climbing 142->153 C, and the 2024 SXR160 reading 60 counts) was decoded with the wrong offset; the SXR160 has a different oil-temp sensor part number so its scaling may differ and should be re-checked against IR separately. Historical context from that water test: PID 0x02 flipped a bit (0x40->0x42) and latched when the OILH warning hit, which looks like a fault/status flag. The real lake overheat that session is now attributed to a corroded eBay exhaust manifold leaking cooling water (found 2026-10-23), not to a scaling artifact.

pids.name: Battery
pids.notes: Re-enabled with a corrected divisor. Previously switched off because PID 0x0A returned 00 00 on an Ultra LX at key-on, and a short 2026-10-13 idle/rev research log on another ski showed it 'frozen' right up to engine shutoff — but 0x0A wasn't a defined/polled channel at the time, so it was only sampled once via the slow extra-PID sweep, not actually confirmed static. A later water-test research log, with 0x0A re-read many times over a 2+ minute ride, shows it tracking RPM: raw 695 (13.63 V) at a 6100 rpm cruise, dropping to raw 654-668 (12.82-13.10 V) at idle, rising again on the next cruise — a charging-system signature (alternator output rises with RPM), and raw/51 lands it right in the 13.0-13.7 V range expected while running. Still just a 4-point fit, not calibrated — confirm against a multimeter on the battery terminals next time out. At key-on/engine-off on a 2024 SXR160 (2026-10-16), 0x0A read 0 too, same as the Ultra LX at key-on — consistent so far, but this ski hasn't been run with 0x0A enabled yet to check the raw/51 scaling against RPM. A 2026-10-19 key-on log on the Android tablet backs up the 'only while the engine turns' pattern: 0x0A read 0 at key-on/engine-off, then 11.59 V while cranking (288 rpm), 9.02 V at the cranking dip and 11.63 V right after, and back to 0 once cranking stopped. So 0 V at key-on is normal for this ECU, not a dead battery; the channel looks live once the engine turns over. 2026-10-21 SXR160 idle/rev log: 9.7-12.1 V cranking, 13.4-13.9 V at idle, 14.27 V at 4300 rpm, 0 with the engine off. The raw/51 scaling fits a charging system on this ski too.
